subject: Logic
title: Well-Formed Formulas
description: Learn Well-Formed Formulas in one minute.

hook.text: Not every string of symbols is meaningful. "P → ∧ Q" is nonsense—formal logic has grammar rules.

buildup.text: A well-formed formula (WFF) follows strict syntax: correct connectives between proper propositions.

discovery.text: "(P ∧ Q) → R" is well-formed. "P ∧ → Q" is not. Parentheses and order matter.

twist.text: Just like natural language needs grammar, formal logic needs syntax to prevent ambiguity and errors.

climax.text: Only WFFs can be evaluated for truth. Ill-formed strings have no truth value—they're just noise.

quiz.question: What is a well-formed formula?
options: A logically correct sentence following syntax rules
